newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-SAMPRAS AND KAFELINKOV TO CLASH IN SWISS SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS AND KAFELINKOV TO CLASH IN SWISS SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Pete Sampras and Yevgeny Kafelnikov both posted quarter-final wins at the Swiss indoor championships on Friday, setting up a semifinal showdown between the U.S. and French Open titleholders.

Sampras, the world number one, playing in his first event since winning his fourth U.S. title, produced his best tennis of the tournament as he neatly disposed of Swede Mikael Tillstrom 6-3 6-4 in just 62 minutes.
But Kafelnikov had to struggle to earn his place, coming back to beat Marc Goellner of Germany 5-7 6-4 6-2.
The Czech Republic's Jiri Novak, who on Thursday upset Australian Open champion Boris Becker, will take on Germany's Hendrik Dreekman in Saturday's other semifinal.
For the first time in the tournament, Sampras was in complete control from the opening serve.

One timely break in the first set to go 4-2 up and another early in the second to lead 2-1 was all he needed to secure a re-match against the player who beat him in the semifinals of the French Open earlier this year, denying the American a shot at the only grand slam title to elude him.
"The way this week's been going I didn't expect anything today," said Sampras, the winner of six titles already this year. "I got off to a good start and my game just started to click.
"Tonight gave me confidence going into tomorrow's match against Kafelnikov."
Unlike Sampras, Kafelnikov has yet to find his rhythm on the Swiss carpet, all three of his matches requiring three sets to decide.
Kafelnikov got off to a disastrous start as Goellner, who only made it into the tournament when Arnaud Boetsch was forced out with a back injury, took the first set and a 4-1 lead in the second.
But the 22-year-old Russian suddenly re-grouped to win the next five games and take the second set. The world number five and third seed then broke a demoralised Goellner twice more in the third.

"To come back like that on a court like this is kind of Houdini-like," said Sampras, the first world number one to play in the event since Bjorn Borg in 1980. "So he must be playing some good tennis. I certainly know what to expect."
Dreekman was also forced to stage a dramatic comeback. Down 5-0 to the Czech Republic's Petr Korda in the first set, Dreekman rebounded to claim a stunning 7-6 (8-6) 6-4 win.
Novak also needed three sets to get past French qualifier Olivier Delaitre 4-6 7-5 6-2.
